blocks.content: Introduction to Manual-first troubleshooting start point
Choose consult-manual as the correct first step in troubleshooting.

items.definition: In a Part 145 shop, the first step when troubleshooting any fault is to consult the manufacturer's maintenance manual — approved data must guide the diagnostic procedure before any components are replaced.
items.analogy: Like calling tech support before replacing your router — diagnosis first, hardware swap last.

blocks.question: A VOR receiver shows an intermittent NAV flag. What is the correct first step in a Part 145 shop?
choices: Consult the manufacturer's maintenance manual before replacing any components
Swap the receiver with a known-good spare to quickly isolate the fault to the LRU
Check the antenna coax for continuity — it is the most common cause of intermittent flags
Document the fault and return the aircraft to service pending parts availability
blocks.feedback: Approved technical data must guide all maintenance in a Part 145 shop. The manual defines the diagnostic procedure — it may direct checking the antenna first or running a self-test. Jumping to a swap without the manual is a regulatory violation regardless of technician experience.
